claim: "The study found 14% more issues per hour, 34% for new staff and no measurable gain for experienced staff" (audit section 3)
problem: The cited paper does not say experienced staff gained nothing. The NBER abstract (w31161) says 34% is for "novice and low-skilled workers" and that the tool had "minimal impact on experienced and highly skilled workers". "No measurable gain" is stronger than the source and "new staff" is a looser category than "novice and low-skilled".
fix: Rewrite as: "The study found 14% more issues resolved per hour on average, 34% for novice and low-skilled agents, and only a small gain for experienced agents; we assume 8-15%."

claim: "500-800 hours of quote prep a year, roughly $12,000-$25,000 ... (Inference: 15-40 requests monthly, 2-6 hours each.)" (audit section 1)
problem: The hours range does not follow from the stated assumptions. 15-40 requests a month at 2-6 hours is 360-2,880 gross hours a year, so the 500-hour low end is above the low end of the stated volume; the reader cannot reproduce the figure without an unstated reduction percentage. The dollar band itself is consistent with the hours and the two NJ wage medians ($22.95/$30.15), so it is not inflated, just unexplained.
fix: Add the missing step, e.g. "(Inference: ~1,000-1,600 gross hours a year from 20-30 requests a month at ~4 hours each; we assume about half is saved.)" or state the cut percentage explicitly.

claim: "500-1,850 hours of client-service capacity, $12,000-$40,000 a year" (audit section 3)
problem: Arithmetic does not reconcile: 500 hours x $22.95 = ~$11,500 and 1,850 hours x $22.95 = ~$42,500, so the stated dollar band is above the low end and below the high end of its own hours. Small, but a CEO who checks will notice.
fix: Use matching figures, e.g. "500-1,750 hours, roughly $11,500-$40,000 a year".

claim: "Yet new business still arrives as a spreadsheet emailed to a general inbox" (opening) and "new business still comes in as a downloaded questionnaire emailed to info@" (email opener)
problem: PDR's pricing page does direct prospects to download the questionnaire and email it to info@, but the contact page also publishes a phone number (732.316.2757) and a web form, so "new business arrives as" states the only intake path as fact and contradicts section 3 of the same document, which lists the phone and inbox as the channels. It also reads as a claim about internals we cannot see.
fix: Attribute it to the site: "the published route to a price is still a downloaded questionnaire emailed to info@" / "your pricing page still sends new enquiries to an Excel questionnaire at info@".

claim: "Even with the client visibility you advertise, businesses like yours often find answers live in one person's memory of a client's SOP." (audit section 3)
problem: The claim that peer 3PLs "often" keep client SOPs in one person's memory has no cited source and reads as an assertion about other companies. The client-visibility half is well sourced (technology page), the second half is not.
fix: Either cite a source or mark it: "our working assumption - not verified for PDR - is that the answer often sits with one experienced person."
